editorial:
Imagine you are a teenager who feels totally ignored by everyone at school. You and your best friend decide to deal with the bullies by making a movie about it. At first, it feels like a goofy home video project with lots of awkward jokes and funny mistakes. You get to see these two kids just hanging out, talking about their dreams, and trying to be creative. The vibe is very loose and real, making you feel like you are watching a real vlog from a couple of kids in the suburbs. It starts off as a lighthearted comedy, but you can tell something darker is brewing under the surface as they get more obsessed with their script.

What really works here is the acting; it feels so natural that you forget they are playing characters. The way the movie shifts from a joke to something scary is a wild ride that will keep you guessing. While the slow start might bore some people, the payoff is totally worth it. If you want to experience this one, you should try renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch or add the Blu-ray to your physical collection if you love indie films. It is a great pick for anyone who likes movies that feel like a documentary but have a shocking twist.
endingExplained: The movie takes a dark turn when you realize the kids aren't just making a fake movie. They actually carry out the violent plan they filmed. The ending shows them committing a school shooting, mirroring the plot of their project. The twist is that the entire movie was a way to document their crime. It ends with the police closing in, leaving you shocked by how the funny friendship turned into a tragedy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found-footage movies and stories about teenage rebellion.
watchReasons: feels like a real home movie
